4. Both parties adduced oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective cases, The learned Munsif on a consideration of the same decreed the suit in part declaring the decision of the Academic Council dated 22.4.74 and 1.7.74 as illegal, void and without jurisdiction and further declare the plaintiff to have passed the 4th year Final Examination held in November 1973. The learned Munsif however rejected the prayer of the plaintiff for declaration that his expulsion on 24.2.75 was illegal and without Jurisdiction. 

 5. On appeal by the defendants the learned Additional District Judge affirmed the Judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif with the modification that the expulsion order passed against the plaintiff by the Chief Supervisor was also declared Illegal and without jurisdiction and accordingly the cross-appeal filed by the plaintiff was allowed. Hence the present appeal at the instance of the defendants. 

 6. It appears that the learned Additional District Judge while affirming the judgment and decree in part did not think it necessary to assign any reason nor did he discuss any evidence. Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly enjoins that the appellate court whether affirming or reversing the decree must give its own reason after assessment of the evidence on record. It is singularly unfortunate that the learned Additional District Judge should have ignored the mandatory provision of Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code. It was incumbent upon him as a final court of fact to discuss and assess the evidence on record and give his own reasons for the finding. 

 14. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the Additional District Judge are hereby set aside and the Case is remanded to the trial court for rehearing in accordance with law. It is further directed that the plaintiff be given an opportunity to amend the plaint within one month of the arrival of the records in the trial court with notice to the parties failing which the suit shall stand dismissed. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case there will be no order as to costs.
